title: orch agent adapters v1 (workspace/src/orch/agents.json)
description: The one place that knows agent tools: how to find one, the argv for a fresh or resumed run (oneshot or live in tmux), how a live run takes input and says it is idle, how session ids are obtained, and capability flags that switch features on or off (the generic adapter is the floor: everything works with all flags false). Only adapters.py reads it. Argv items may hold the placeholders {prompt} {session} {new_session} {orch_hooks_file} {allow}; the string "{command}" / "{interactive}" in place of an argv means the user's [agents.<name>] command, split with shlex. A oneshot argv without {prompt} gets the prompt appended (prompt_via arg). User entries in .orch/config.toml are described by $defs/user_config (local-files.md).

argv.description: Argument safety (prevents bugs, not agents): {prompt} is its own item AFTER a '--' item, so text starting with '-' is never read as an option (or the prompt goes on stdin: prompt_via stdin and no {prompt}). {session} is bound as --flag={session}, follows its flag, or is a positional before '--'; session ids never start with '-' (ticket.schema.json sessions[].id). The order is checked by validate.py and by adapters.py at load.

signal.description: hook:<Event> = the tool's own hook calls `orch run event`; orch:run-done = the agent runs `orch run done` itself.

label.description: Shown to people. "{name}" = the user's entry name.

store_args.description: Optional, built-in adapters only (orch ignores it elsewhere). For a tool sandboxed to its working folder: when the agent works in a separate copy of the project, `--add-dir <workspace>/.orch` is inserted into the oneshot argv after the template word `after`, so the workspace's own store stays writable. Nothing else is allowed here: exactly `--add-dir` and `{store}` once.

env_any.description: Any set = orch runs inside this tool (labels agent:<name>).

resume.description: null = cannot resume: every run starts fresh from the ticket and its summary.

stream_args.description: Optional. Added for a machine-readable event stream.

allow_args.description: Optional. Added to retry with a tool allowed ({allow}).

send.description: How input goes in: orch types one fixed ASCII line (send-keys -l) telling the agent to run `orch run input <ticket>`, then Enter as its own key. A person's text never reaches the screen.

prompt_box.description: Optional, default true. True: the tool draws a bordered prompt box; orch types its notice only into a box it can see and proves empty, else it waits. False: a plain command-line tool; the cursor's own line is its prompt (and any doubt waits).

dialog.description: Optional. Case-insensitive multi-line regex for the tool's own dialogs (permission prompts): while one shows anywhere on the pane, orch never sends Enter.

interrupt_keys.description: tmux send-keys names that stop the current turn.

idle_notice.description: Optional. An attention hook whose input matches is the tool saying it waits at its prompt (idle, input may go in). Anything else from that hook is attention: nothing is pasted.

fields.description: Top-level string fields of the hook input that are checked.

events.description: Name of the event normaliser for this tool's transcript/stream, or null (board from ticket changes only).

trust.description: Optional. The tool asks once per folder whether to trust it, before any hook runs. orch sets this one JSON key to true before a live start (read, merge, re-read, atomic replace; an unreadable or missing file is never touched).

file.description: JSON file, relative to the folder named by dir_env, else the home folder.

path.description: Keys to the boolean; "{folder}" = the workspace's full path.

screens.description: Optional. Screens the tool shows before it is up (no hook fires), checked in order, the first match counts. Only read while a live run is still starting. A screen with answer is a harmless first-run screen: the run's own wrapper sends those keys to its own pane, at most once per screen per run, and logs it on the ticket. A screen without answer (a login, anything else) is shown as a plain status line and nothing is typed.

match.description: Case-insensitive regex for the pane text.

say.description: Plain words for people; {label} and {ticket} are filled in. Shown when the screen is not answered.

answer.description: Optional. tmux send-keys names that pass this screen (never a login or a permission prompt).

what.description: With answer: plain words for the ticket history, e.g. "folder trust".

folder.description: With answer: only when the run's folder is a workspace set up with `orch init` (its consent) and the screen names that folder.

live.description: null = no live mode; runs are oneshot.

permissions.description: Optional. Flags for the workspace's permission mode (kept per machine in the orch home (permissions.json), set by orch config set workspace.permissions, never read from .orch/config.toml: ask | auto (default) | full), added to every oneshot and live start. An adapter without this ignores the mode. A mode that is missing adds nothing.

oneOf.description: The flags (empty = the tool's own default).
Flags that depend on the installed tool: args when its --help text contains if_help_has, else the flags in else.

hooks.description: Tool hook event -> the orch command it runs. orch writes them into a per-run file ({orch_hooks_file}).

id.description: chosen-by-orch = orch passes {new_session}; from-output = read from the run's output; none = no sessions.

hand_started.description: How a session started by hand reports its id, or null.

parse.description: For from-output: name of the output parser.

missing.description: Optional. Case-insensitive regex for the tool's output when a resumed session does not exist. Only then does orch start fresh; any other failure is a failure. Absent = never falls back.

transcript.description: Optional. Where the tool saves a session's conversation. A session whose folder exists but whose file does not is never resumed (it starts fresh), and a new session id is kept only once its file exists.

dir_env.description: Environment variable naming the tool's folder; else home is used.

home.description: The tool's folder in the person's home.

path.description: Parts below the folder: {folder} = the workspace path with every other character than A-Z, a-z, 0-9 as '-'; the last part {session}.<ext>.

interactive_tmux.description: For generic: true only when the user entry sets interactive.

instructions.description: File the tool reads by itself (AGENTS.md).

instructions_link.description: File -> line it must contain, e.g. TOOL.md -> @AGENTS.md (the file this tool reads at start).

files.description: Files orch prepares so this tool finds AGENTS.md and the skills.

user_config.description: The agent part of .orch/config.toml, parsed (other tables belong to add-ons and are not checked here).

agent.description: Which agent does the work here: an adapter name or an [agents.<name>] entry.

live_idle_minutes.description: A live session idle (or waiting for a person), or on a ticket that has been Done, this long is closed on the next orch run call; its session id stays, so Continue resumes. Default 60.

code.description: Workspace code for ticket keys (<code>-<n>, e.g. DM1-12): 2-4 uppercase letters or digits. Set by orch init (suggested from the folder name, or --code), changed with orch config set workspace.code; a change never rewrites old keys.

adapter.description: Built-in adapter whose rules apply, e.g. generic.

command.description: Oneshot command line ({prompt} optional; appended when missing). Used without confirmation; the first use on a machine prints one notice line.

interactive.description: Optional command that starts the tool interactively (live runs in tmux).

prompt.description: Optional. How the command takes the task: arg (default; {prompt}, or appended after '--' when missing) or stdin.
